support_status: Ubuntu 24.04 CPU build and clean wheel installation validated on isolated compatibility branch; no portable Linux PyPI wheel or CUDA claim

runs.last_step: Fetch the same pinned Boost headers as Windows
runs.finding: Boost archive checksum passed; unzip failed because build/boost parent directory did not exist.
runs.remediation: Create build/boost before unzip; applied on ci/linux-bootstrap.

runs.finding: CMake configure and initial GCC compilation succeeded; compilation stopped at ATen/functorch/Interpreter.h include nlohmann/json.hpp, which the Torch wheel does not supply. The prior local Windows environment supplied nlohmann/json 3.11.2 through ambient Conda include headers.
runs.remediation: Pin and verify nlohmann/json 3.11.2 as an explicit shared build dependency, include its MIT notice, rebuild and repeat CI.

runs.finding: Pinned JSON 3.11.2 download/hash verification and CMake configure succeeded. GCC reached 6 percent native compilation, then rejected unqualified QuantLib parameter types in generated cross-namespace friend declarations in triplebandlinearop.hpp. Errors include FdmLinearOpComposite, BoundaryConditionSchemeHelper, Array, Time and Real not declared.
runs.remediation: A separate Linux compatibility experiment can qualify generated friend parameter types; no numerical algorithm change is indicated. Current supported scope remains Windows only.

runs.last_step: Build native Linux package (post-build import probe)
runs.finding: Isolated namespace qualification fixed GCC compilation. Native target compiled and linked at 100 percent. Mandatory load probe then failed with undefined symbol QuantLib::DiscretizedOption::postAdjustValuesImpl(), implemented in omitted upstream source ql/discretizedasset.cpp.
runs.remediation: Review adding the original pinned source translation unit to the explicit source closure on the isolated Linux branch; do not link a stock QuantLib library.
runs.generated_overlay_check: All 84 generated files match the prior output after removing only the added namespace qualifiers in four friend declarations across three headers; compatibility diff emitted separately.

runs.finding: Generated friend namespace qualification and inclusion of original pinned ql/discretizedasset.cpp permit complete Linux native compilation, import, full regression, wheel packaging, dependency inspection and isolated installation. Changes remain isolated from the Windows release candidate.
runs.runtime_dependencies: libtorch_cpu.so and libc10.so are supplied by the declared torch package. Development-tree ldd reports not found because installed relative RPATH does not point into the build interpreter; independent installed package import and pricing passed.
limitations: Validated only on the build distribution, Ubuntu 24.04.
No manylinux container build, repair, or oldest claimed distribution check.
Workflow retains validation evidence only; experimental wheel was not uploaded or published.

interpretation: The workflow uses continue-on-error, so job outcomes must be inspected separately from the workflow badge. The first four jobs failed as recorded. The fifth isolated-branch job passed all configured native, regression, wheel, auditwheel and external-installation steps. This establishes Ubuntu 24.04 CPU development compatibility only; no portable Linux distribution is published or advertised.
next_step: Review the two isolated compatibility commits before integrating. Preserve the Windows-only initial PyPI wheel scope unless a pinned manylinux build, dependency policy, and oldest-distribution clean install are completed separately. Keep Linux CUDA unsupported until measured.
